paragraphs.title: Joab’s Ruse and the Woman of Tekoa

answers: The king’s heart was toward Absalom
The king was angry with Absalom
The king wanted to go to war
easy.explanation: Joab perceived that the king’s heart was toward Absalom.
easy.q: What did Joab perceive about David?

easy.explanation: Joab fetched a wise woman from Tekoa.
easy.q: Where did Joab find the wise woman?

easy.explanation: Joab told her to feign herself to be a mourner.
easy.q: What did Joab tell the woman to pretend to be?

answers: To appear to be grieving for the dead
medium.explanation: The mourning clothing supported the story she was to tell the king.
medium.q: Why did Joab tell the woman to wear mourning apparel?

answers: He wrote them for the king
He put them in her mouth
He told them to the people
medium.explanation: The passage says that Joab put the words in her mouth.
medium.q: What did Joab do with the words she was to speak?

answers: Clothing worn by one grieving for the dead
medium.explanation: Mourning apparel is clothing associated with grief for the dead.

answers: He worked indirectly instead of speaking to David directly
He gave up trying to influence David
He left the decision to the people
challenge.explanation: Joab used the woman and a prepared story to influence David indirectly.
challenge.q: What does Joab’s method show about how he acted?

answers: They caused David to leave Jerusalem
They gave Joab a reason to seek Absalom’s return
They caused Absalom to come alone

challenge.q: Why was the woman especially suited for this task?

paragraphs.title: The Widow and Her Two Sons

easy.explanation: She fell before David and said, “Help, O king.”
easy.q: How did the woman first address David?

easy.explanation: She said that she was a widow and that her husband was dead.
easy.q: What happened to the woman’s husband?

easy.explanation: The woman said that she had two sons.
easy.q: How many sons did the woman have?

medium.explanation: The brothers strove together in the field, and one slew the other.
medium.q: What caused one of the woman’s sons to die?

answers: He should be sent to Geshur
He should be killed as an act of vengeance
medium.explanation: The family wanted the surviving son delivered so they could kill him.
medium.q: What did the family want done to the surviving son?

answers: One who seeks vengeance for a person killed
One who brings water to a family
medium.explanation: A revenger of blood seeks vengeance for someone who was killed.

answers: She would immediately lose her house
No son would remain to continue the family
She would have to leave Tekoa
challenge.explanation: The son was the heir and the family’s remaining hope.
challenge.q: Why would the son’s death destroy the widow’s future?

answers: His life would preserve the family name and inheritance
He promised to become a soldier
The family wanted to move to Jerusalem
challenge.explanation: She said that killing him would destroy the heir and quench the family’s remaining coal.
challenge.q: What main reason did the woman give for sparing her son?

answers: He promised to protect her and give charge concerning her
challenge.explanation: David promised that no one would harm her.
challenge.q: What was David’s first response to her request?

easy.explanation: Her story was meant to make David consider Absalom.
easy.q: Whom did the woman want David to think about?

answers: Not one hair of his head would fall to the earth
He would be sent to Geshur
His family would decide his fate
easy.explanation: David promised that not one hair of her son would fall to the earth.
easy.q: What did David say would happen to the woman’s son?

easy.explanation: She admitted that Joab had put the words in her mouth.
easy.q: Who was behind the woman’s words?

answers: It is like water spilt on the ground that cannot be gathered again
It is like a locked gate
It is like a battle that continues
medium.explanation: She compared death to water spilled on the ground.
medium.q: What comparison did the woman make about death?

medium.explanation: A banished person has been driven away or kept from home.
medium.q: What does “banished” mean in this passage?

answers: To move him to do the true thing
medium.explanation: She hoped the king would perform her request and bring home the banished.
medium.q: Why did the woman say she had come to David?

answers: If David protected her son, he should also consider his banished son
If David punished her son, he should punish Joab
If David saved her son, he should go to war
challenge.explanation: Her parable urged David to apply the same mercy to Absalom.
challenge.q: What connection did the woman make between David’s judgment and Absalom?

answers: He suspected that the story had been arranged
He wanted to appoint Joab as judge
The woman had asked to meet Joab
challenge.explanation: David recognized that the woman’s words concealed a planned purpose.
challenge.q: Why did David ask whether Joab was involved?

answers: God does not desire that the banished remain lost
Only a king may decide matters of life and death
challenge.explanation: She emphasized that God devises means so that the banished are not finally lost.
challenge.q: What idea about God appears in the woman’s argument?

easy.explanation: David told Joab to bring Absalom again.
easy.q: What did David command Joab to do?

easy.explanation: Joab went to Geshur and brought Absalom to Jerusalem.
easy.q: From where did Joab bring Absalom?

easy.explanation: David let Absalom return home but did not permit him to see the king’s face.
easy.q: Did David allow Absalom to see his face?

answers: Absalom returned to Jerusalem but was not reconciled with David
medium.explanation: Absalom returned, but David still kept his distance.
medium.q: What was the result of Joab’s counsel?

medium.explanation: Absalom was brought back physically, but the relationship remained broken.
medium.q: What does the combination of returning home and not seeing the king’s face show?

medium.explanation: David commanded Joab to bring Absalom back.
medium.q: What does “bring ... again” mean in David’s command?

answers: The distance between father and son remained
Joab refused to speak with David
challenge.explanation: Absalom returned to the city, but David still refused to see him.
challenge.q: What emotional tension remained after Absalom’s return?

answers: He allowed Absalom’s return but not a meeting
He allowed a meeting but not a return
He rejected both the return and the meeting
challenge.explanation: David accepted Absalom’s return while withholding his presence.

answers: He initiated and carried out Absalom’s return
He worked to keep Absalom away
challenge.explanation: Joab arranged the plan and then brought Absalom from Geshur.
challenge.q: What does Joab’s role show at this point?

answers: There was no blemish in him
easy.explanation: The text says there was no blemish in him from foot to head.
easy.q: How does the passage describe Absalom’s appearance?

easy.explanation: His hair was heavy, and he weighed it after cutting it.
easy.q: What was remarkable about Absalom’s hair?

easy.explanation: Absalom dwelt two full years in Jerusalem without seeing the king’s face.
easy.q: How long did Absalom live in Jerusalem without seeing David?

answers: He covered it with a garment
medium.explanation: He polled his head when the hair became heavy.
medium.q: What did Absalom do when his hair became heavy?

medium.explanation: Absalom had a daughter named Tamar.
medium.q: Who was Tamar in this passage?

medium.explanation: Absalom was greatly admired for his beauty.
medium.q: What does “praised” mean in the description of Absalom’s beauty?

answers: Great outward beauty alongside prolonged separation from David
challenge.explanation: The passage highlights his beauty while also noting his separation from David.
challenge.q: What contrast is emphasized in Absalom’s situation?

answers: His outward appearance received special attention
challenge.explanation: The text gives unusual detail about the weight and cutting of his hair.
challenge.q: What does the detail about Absalom’s hair suggest?

answers: It shows that his separation from David continued for a long time
It proves that Absalom left Jerusalem
It shows that David forgot him
challenge.explanation: Two full years without a meeting emphasize the continuing estrangement.
challenge.q: How does the two-year period affect our understanding of Absalom’s situation?

paragraphs.title: Confrontation with Joab and Reconciliation with David

easy.explanation: Absalom sent for Joab to send him to the king.
easy.q: Whom did Absalom send for help in contacting David?

easy.explanation: Absalom ordered his servants to set Joab’s field on fire.
easy.q: What did Absalom tell his servants to do to Joab’s field?

easy.explanation: After Absalom bowed before him, David kissed him.
easy.q: What did David do at the end of the passage?

answers: To make Joab come to him
medium.explanation: The burning forced Joab to come and respond to Absalom.
medium.q: Why did Absalom burn Joab’s field?

answers: He wanted to see the king’s face, and if he had iniquity, David could kill him
medium.explanation: Absalom asked to see David and said that David could kill him if he was guilty.
medium.q: What did Absalom want Joab to tell David?

medium.explanation: Joab’s field was a piece of land where barley grew.
medium.q: What is a “field” in this context?

answers: He used a drastic action to force Joab to respond
He gave up trying to see David
He asked the people to replace David
challenge.explanation: Absalom used the fire to compel Joab to come to him.
challenge.q: What does the burning of the field reveal about Absalom’s method?

answers: At first he could not see David, but at the end he stood before him
At first he was in Geshur, and at the end he returned there
At first he was fighting, and at the end he won a battle
challenge.explanation: After Joab spoke to David, Absalom was summoned into the king’s presence.
challenge.q: How did Absalom’s situation change from the beginning to the end?

answers: Outwardly, the relationship between father and son was restored
David announced that Absalom would immediately reign
challenge.explanation: The kiss signals an outward reconciliation, though it does not prove every tension disappeared.
challenge.q: What is the likely significance of David’s kiss?
